title: Hybrids Carry October U.S. Auto Sales as Toyota and Hyundai Gain and Ford Slips
dek: Hybrid demand and retail buyers pushed Toyota, Honda, Hyundai and Kia to October gains, while Ford fell behind the market's lift.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Exterior of a car dealership showroom on a city street

keyPoints: Automotive News reported that U.S. sales rose 6.5% in October at Toyota Motor Corp., with the Toyota division up 5.7% and Lexus up 12%.
Hyundai Motor America reported record October total sales of 73,452, up 5%, and retail sales of 62,646, up 9%, per its Nov. 3 release.
Hyundai's hybrid sales rose 20% in October and made up 29% of its volume; its year-to-date hybrid sales are up 50%.
Automotive News said Ford slipped in October while Toyota, Honda, Hyundai and Kia gained on retail demand.
Carpro's October roundup said Honda's electrified sales, mostly hybrids, rose 11% to 33,760.
body:
October was a good month for the Japanese and Korean automakers that lean on hybrids. Automotive News reported that Toyota Motor Corp. sold 6.5% more vehicles in the U.S. last month, with the Toyota brand up 5.7% and Lexus up 12%. The trade publication said Honda, Hyundai and Kia also posted gains, helped by retail buyers. Ford was the notable laggard.

## Hyundai's numbers

Hyundai Motor America reported its best October on record, with 73,452 vehicles sold, a 5% increase from October 2025. Retail sales, which exclude fleet deals, rose 9% to 62,646. The company credited the Santa Fe, Kona, IONIQ 5, Elantra and Palisade, and said its hybrid lineup grew 20% to make up 29% of its October volume. Year to date, Hyundai's hybrid sales are up 50%.

## Why hybrids matter

The pattern fits a market that is buying efficiency without fully committing to battery-electric cars. Hybrids let buyers avoid charging while cutting fuel costs, and they have become a fast-growing share of the sales mix for several brands. Hyundai's own release frames the shift as a choice across SUVs, hybrids and EVs rather than a single move away from gasoline.

## The wider picture

Automotive News describes the month as a mix of retail buyers and fleet deliveries, and said the overall market benefited from an extra selling day and a comparison with a weaker October 2025. Part of the gain is therefore calendar-driven rather than a clean trend. Carpro's roundup also pointed to Honda's electrified sales, which are mostly hybrids, rising 11% to 33,760 units.

Hyundai used its release to highlight new product: an all-new Tucson with a next-generation hybrid system targeting up to 42 mpg, and about $450 million of investment at its Montgomery, Alabama plant for future vehicles and propulsion technology. Hybrid share is now a product-cycle question as much as a demand question.

## What to watch

The October figures arrive before the holiday shopping season and before the full-year comparisons carmakers tend to emphasize in fourth-quarter reports. Investors will look for whether Toyota's hybrid strength holds through November, and whether Ford can close the gap in its truck and SUV lineup.

marketImpact.summary: Strong hybrid and retail sales support the case that Toyota's mix is working. Ford's October slip is a smaller negative signal, and one month of unit sales does not settle either company's margin outlook.
marketImpact.timeframe: Next 1-2 weeks, until November sales and fourth-quarter guidance commentary arrive
